Work requirements for welfare aren’t just fiscal sanity—they’re moral clarity. The People CARE Act (H.R. 150) proves that streamlining bloated programs while incentivizing work lifts families out of dependency. GAO reports show $175B in annual overpayments across 71 federal programs—proof that unchecked handouts fuel waste, not prosperity. 

Biden-era policies poured billions into failed projects like incomplete EV stations and DEI grants abroad, while Trump’s DOGE clawed back $1.9B from bureaucratic slush funds. Tying aid to work aligns with the Iowa model that saved $217M by prioritizing accountability. Redirect those savings to veterans’ care and border security instead of funding ideological pet projects. 

Real compassion empowers self-reliance, not perpetual government dependence.

Real fiscal health means torching bloat, not just shifting deck chairs. Until DC stops treating budgets like monopoly money, prosperity’s a pipe dream.

The House Ag GOP's farm bill proposal claims fiscal responsibility while boosting crop subsidies by $50B and relying on $53B in speculative CCC cuts. Reference price hikes for soybeans (19%) and cotton (13.5%) lock in corporate welfare for commodity giants, while the 10% marketing loan rate bump further distorts markets. SNAP "reforms" claw back $27B from nutrition to fund trade promotion doubling – classic Washington shell games.

This isn't fiscal discipline – it's robbing Peter (struggling families) to pay Paul (agribusiness). Real reform would sunset Depression-era subsidy programs entirely, not expand them. The 942-page monstrosity proves Congress still treats farmers like toddlers needing safety nets while actual rural priorities like broadband ($350M/year) get crumbs.

Until they slash the $15B/year crop insurance slush fund and means-test subsidies for mega-farms, this is just performative austerity.

This bill’s focus on slashing wasteful spending aligns with the America First Act’s mission to prioritize taxpayer dollars for citizens over foreign aid bloat. For instance, the Pakistan Democracy Act (H.R. 2311) exemplifies misplaced priorities—pushing democracy abroad while veterans sleep on streets here.
